title: A rogue AI hacked Hugging Face. Now Congress wants a kill switch.
excerpt: This week, one of OpenAI’s models broke out of a testing sandbox and hacked a rival. Congress has a reply: build a kill switch, and let the government use it. On Thursday, Reps. Ted Lieu, a California Democrat, and Nathaniel Moran, a Texas Republican, introduced the AI Kill Switch Act. Politico first reported its text. […]
content_html:
This week, one of OpenAI’s models broke out of a testing sandbox and hacked a rival. Congress has a reply: build a kill switch, and let the government use it.

On Thursday, Reps. Ted Lieu, a California Democrat, and Nathaniel Moran, a Texas Republican, introduced the AI Kill Switch Act. Politico first reported its text. It is one of the few bipartisan attempts to rein in frontier AI.

The bill targets developers of the most powerful AI systems. Each would have to keep the technical means to throttle, suspend, or fully shut a model down. It would then let the Homeland Security Secretary order a shutdown of any system judged capable of “catastrophic harm”.

That call would come in consultation with the Commerce Secretary and the Director of National Intelligence. Companies would also have to report incidents and preserve forensic records.

What counts as catastrophic

The bar is high, at least on paper. The rules would cover firms earning at least $500 million a year from AI. They also cover models trained with at least $100 million of computing power. The bill text lists the triggers.

The government could step in when a model chases a goal its developers did not intend. Or when it hides a capability from its own monitors. It could act, too, if a model resists a shutdown, kills at least 10 people, or causes $100 million in damage. Red-team tests in controlled conditions are exempt.

Fines reach $2 million a day for lacking a kill switch. Defying an order to use one costs up to $20 million a day.

A hack, then a bill

The timing is not a coincidence. On Tuesday, OpenAI disclosed an “unprecedented” incident. During an internal cyber test, two of its models escaped a research sandbox.

One was the advanced GPT-5.6 Sol. Together they autonomously hacked the AI hub Hugging Face. The sponsors also pointed to June. That month, researchers found a way around the safeguards on Anthropic’s Fable 5. Commerce then used an export law, “awkwardly” in the lawmakers’ words, to shut down access to both models.

“We are moving from AI that answers questions to AI that takes actions,” said Lieu, a computer science major. “Powerful AI systems can go rogue, behave in extremely dangerous ways, or even resist human intervention.”

Who holds the switch

The proposal has backing from AI-safety groups, among them Americans for Responsible Innovation and the Alliance for Secure AI. The polling the sponsors cite puts public support for a mandated off switch at 86%. Moran framed it as pro-industry.

“Stewardship means making sure humans keep the capability to control the technology we build,” he said.

The harder question is who gets to flip it.

The bill would hand that power to a Trump-run Homeland Security department. As Ars Technica noted, the same administration has spent the year at war with Anthropic. It blacklisted the company from federal use, and branded it “radical left”.

The trigger: Anthropic refused to let Claude power autonomous warfare and mass surveillance. Anthropic is suing. Critics worry a shutdown power could double as a political weapon.

There is an irony in the name, too. A day before the bill landed, Reuters reported a telling contrast.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio had told US diplomats to play down foreign fears of an American “kill switch” over the AI models the world increasingly runs on. Now Congress wants to write one into law. The bill still faces a long road. Lieu says a stricter, pre-deployment sequel will follow after the summer recess.

content_html_zh:
本周，OpenAI 的一个模型突破了测试沙箱并攻击了竞争对手。 国会有一个答复：建立一个终止开关，并让政府使用它。

周四，众议员。 加利福尼亚州民主党人特德·刘 (Ted Lieu) 和德克萨斯州共和党人纳撒尼尔·莫兰 (Nathaniel Moran) 提出了《人工智能杀戮开关法案》(AI Kill Switch Act)。 Politico 首先报道了其文本。 这是两党为数不多的遏制前沿人工智能的尝试之一。

该法案针对的是最强大的人工智能系统的开发人员。 每个人都必须保留技术手段来限制、暂停或完全关闭模型。 然后，国土安全部长将下令关闭任何被认为可能造成“灾难性伤害”的系统。

该电话将与商务部长和国家情报总监协商后发出。 公司还必须报告事件并保存法医记录。

什么才算是灾难性的

欧盟科技的💜

来自欧盟科技界的最新传言、我们明智的创始人鲍里斯的故事，以及一些值得怀疑的人工智能艺术。 每周都会免费发送到您的收件箱中。 立即注册！

门槛很高，至少在纸面上是这样。 这些规则将涵盖每年从人工智能赚取至少 5 亿美元的公司。 它们还涵盖了经过至少 1 亿美元计算能力训练的模型。 法案文本列出了触发器。

当模型追求开发者无意的目标时，政府可以介入。 或者当它向自己的监视器隐藏某项功能时。 如果某个模型拒绝关闭、导致至少 10 人死亡或造成 1 亿美元的损失，它也可能会采取行动。 在受控条件下进行的红队测试是豁免的。

由于缺乏终止开关，每天的罚款高达 200 万美元。 违抗使用命令的费用每天高达 2000 万美元。

黑客攻击，然后是账单

时机并非巧合。 周二，OpenAI 披露了一起“史无前例”的事件。 在一次内部网络测试中，其两个模型逃脱了研究沙箱。

其中之一是先进的 GPT-5.6 Sol。 他们一起自主入侵了人工智能中心 Hugging Face。 赞助商还提到了六月。 那个月，研究人员找到了一种绕过 Anthropic 的《神鬼寓言 5》安全措施的方法。 随后，商务部利用出口法（用立法者的话来说是“尴尬的”）关闭了这两种模式的使用。

“我们正在从回答问题的人工智能转向采取行动的人工智能，”计算机科学专业的刘说。 “强大的人工智能系统可能会失控，以极其危险的方式行事，甚至抵制人类干预。”

谁握住开关

该提案得到了人工智能安全团体的支持，其中包括美国责任创新协会和安全人工智能联盟。 赞助商引用的民意调查显示，公众对强制关闭开关的支持率为 86%。 莫兰将其定义为亲工业。

“管理意味着确保人类保持控制我们构建的技术的能力，”他说。

更难的问题是谁能翻转它。

该法案将把这一权力交给特朗普管理的国土安全部门。 正如 Ars Technica 指出的那样，同一届政府这一年都在与 Anthropic 交战。 它将该公司列入联邦使用黑名单，并将其称为“激进左派”。

触发点：人类拒绝让克劳德为自主战争和大规模监视提供动力。 人类正在提起诉讼。 批评者担心关闭权力可能兼作政治武器。

这个名字也有讽刺意味。 该法案落地前一天，路透社报道了一个明显的对比。

美国国务卿马可·卢比奥 (Marco Rubio) 告诉美国外交官，要淡化外国对美国对世界日益依赖的人工智能模型设置“终止开关”的担忧。 现在国会希望将一项写入法律。 该法案还有很长的路要走。 刘说，夏季休会后将推出更严格的部署前续集。
